_comment: Declarative chat accounts — DOCUMENTATION ONLY; these are not provisioned.
Thunderbird enumerates chat accounts from its account manager: imAccounts.sys.mjs
initAccounts() reads MailServices.accounts, and a chat account is a MailServices
account whose incoming server is type 'im' with imAccount = account<N> (numeric).
Writing the messenger.account.<key>.* prefs alone creates nothing (verified against
Thunderbird 155: blist.sqlite.accounts stays empty). Registering the account would
mean pinning mail.accountmanager.accounts in user.js, which overrides Thunderbird's
own account management and would drop any account added later in the UI — so it is
A chat account (credential-free IRC included) therefore has to be added once in
Thunderbird's own Chat tab; omarchy-thunderbird-chat then reports what exists.
This file records the accounts you intend to add.
name       display name shown in the Chat tab
username   optional; for IRC the nick, or nick@server
